item.title: Decoding the Right-to-Repair Debate
item.description: The right-to-repair debate, concerning who controls U.S. defense IP, has become a contentious issue in defense acquisition policy. Lawmakers need to balance the military’s push for greater access to technical data and industry’s fear of losing revenue and IP control.

item.title: FY 2027 Defense Funding: Potential Post-Midterm Outcomes
item.description: Congress has a full post-midterm agenda, with action needed to fund the Department of Defense and federal government and reconciliation legislation to consider. Seamus Daniels lays out the factors that will shape FY 2027 defense funding decisions after the midterms.

item.title: States Weekly: October 28, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers October 28, 2026.

item.title: Business Support for Human Rights Defenders in an Era of Government Retrenchment
item.description: Human rights defenders are vital partners for businesses operating around the globe. Civic space and the business operating environment are fundamentally intertwined. Businesses should, can, and have supported HRDs in their important work, and such support is more needed than ever.

item.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper—Revised Version
item.description: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch discusses the administration’s challenges in implementing some elements of its trade policies.

item.title: New Zealand’s Two-Track China Policy
item.description: New Zealand is hardening its stance toward China as security concerns mount, but deep economic dependence on Beijing limits how far Wellington can realign with its Western partners.

item.title: The FCC Covered List: National Security, Economic Policy, and Technology Supply Chains
item.description: The FCC’s Covered List has expanded beyond specific high-risk suppliers to restrict entire categories of foreign-produced technology. What does this shift mean for U.S. national security, domestic businesses, and global technology supply chains?

item.title: Did the United States and Russia Just Agree to Collaborate on Data Centers?
item.description: A joint data center proposed as part of broader negotiations between the United States and Russia poses a substantive threat to U.S. national security. Congress should play a vital role in scrutinizing the idea before it becomes a reality.

item.title: Ukraine and South Korea’s Diplomatic Dispute Deepens | State of Play
item.description: Victor Cha explains why the diplomatic dispute between South Korea and Ukraine over President Volodymyr Zelensky’s public disclosure that Kyiv had transferred two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul has deepened, and what both sides may want out of it.
